h1: Gate Repair in Dallas: Walk Gates, Driveway Gates and Automatic Openers
heroSub: Sagging, dragging, latching badly or an opener that stops halfway: most gate faults break into a few known parts. Call now at (214) 555-0137 and compare two or three written quotes.
introHtml:
Gate repair in Dallas usually comes down to one of three faults: the gate has moved (sag, drag, a post that shifted), the hardware has worn (hinges, latch, drop rod), or the automation has failed (opener, sensors, power, remote). Each has a different fix and sometimes a different tradesperson, so sorting out which one you have keeps you from paying for the wrong repair.

White Rock Fence Co is an advertising site, not a contractor. It does not do the work; it connects Dallas-area homeowners with independent fence and gate contractors who quote the job. This page sets out the failure modes, the equipment classes and what belongs in a written quote, with every price attributed to the firm that publishes it. Call (214) 555-0137 to get started.

features.title: Sagging and dragging gates
features.desc: A gate that scrapes the ground usually has a shifted post, a racked frame or worn hinges. The contractor diagnoses which before touching the hardware.

features.title: Hinges, latches and drop rods
features.desc: Hardware is the cheapest part of a gate job. One Dallas-area firm lists a latch or hinge fix at $60 to $150.

features.title: Openers that stop or reverse
features.desc: Photo-eyes, limit settings, batteries, remotes and the power supply are the usual suspects. Ask the contractor to name the one that failed.

features.title: Swing, slide and cantilever
features.desc: Each class of driveway gate needs different room, posts and foundation work. Compare quotes for the same class, width and opener.

features.title: Wood and iron gates
features.desc: Wood leaves tend to sag over time. Iron leaves are heavier and load the posts and hinges harder, so the post work matters more.

features.title: Power, permits and HOA
features.desc: Power wiring for an opener is electrical work, so ask who holds the electrical license. Confirm permit and HOA rules before you commit.

sections.heading: How a gate fault gets diagnosed
sections.html:
A contractor working through a gate problem normally goes in one order: post and frame first, hardware second, automation last. A gate that drags is rarely fixed by a new latch, and an opener that strains is often fighting a gate that has sagged. Keeping to that order stops you paying for an opener repair when the real fault is a leaning post.

  • Drags on the ground or rubs the post: the post has moved, the frame has racked or the hinges have worn. The repair is a reset post, a re-squared frame or new hinges.
  • Latch will not catch: usually the same sag, seen at the latch side. The gate gets aligned first, then the latch and strike are adjusted or replaced.
  • Opener stops partway or reverses: commonly the photo-eyes, the limit settings, or something binding in the gate's path. Ask the contractor to say which it was.
  • Opener will not close or does not respond: remote and keypad batteries, the backup battery and the power supply get checked before anyone talks about replacing the motor.

This page gives no service interval because none is sourced. Ask the contractor what inspection schedule they recommend for your gate type, and have it written into the quote.

sections.heading: Equipment classes: swing, slide and cantilever gates
sections.html:
Driveway gates come in three working classes. A swing gate hangs on hinges and needs room to open across the drive. A track slide gate rolls on a ground track and needs a clear run alongside the fence line. A cantilever slide rolls without a ground track and is the premium class. For the iron versions of each, see the iron fence page.

Published Dallas-area prices for a new automatic gate: TX Fence & Deck (page modified 28 Sep 2026) lists swing at $3,500 to $7,000, track slide at $4,500 to $8,500 and cantilever slide at $5,500 to $10,000, and says most residential automatic gate installs in the Dallas area run $3,500 to $10,000. The same firm says running power to a remote gate can add $500 to $2,000. Everlast Gates & Fence, a Dallas-Fort Worth firm, puts foundation and track work for a sliding gate at $600 to $1,500.

An opener added to an existing gate is $800 to $2,000 on one TX Fence & Deck page, and Fixr's national guide puts openers at $400 to $5,000. These are what individual firms advertise, not this site's quotes, and one firm's pages do not always agree with each other. Compare quotes that name the same gate class, width and opener, and see the fence cost page and fence installation page for the wider picture.

sections.heading: What gate repairs cost, from published pages
sections.html:
No Dallas firm we found publishes a gate service-call fee, so ask whether a first visit is billed before you book. What firms do publish is per-repair ranges, listed here with the firm that states each.

  • Latch or hinge fix: $60 to $150 (TX Fence & Deck, 30 Jun 2026).
  • Gate hardware and drop, and separately a gate rebuild: $400 to $1,200 each (Roof Raiders & Co, Dallas). Ft Worth Fence & Patio, in Fort Worth, lists gate rebuilds at $250 to $850.
  • Automatic gate repair: $150 to $600, extensive work $2,500 or more. Opener repair $150 to $400, motor repair $200 to $600, motor replacement $500 to $1,200, tracks and rollers $100 to $350 (Viking Fence, Austin).
  • Problems caught early: $100 to $300 to fix, with motor replacements at $1,000+ (TX Fence & Deck).

Everlast Gates & Fence, citing Angi's national data, says the average automatic gate repair is about $900, with many jobs between $550 and $1,500. The spread between firms is wide, which is the reason to get two or three written quotes for the same fault. For wood and panel work, see the fence repair page.

sections.heading: Writing the quote and checking the rules
sections.html:
A quote you can compare names the gate class and width, the post and hinge or track work, the opener make and model, and what comes with it: photo-eyes, backup battery and a stated number of remotes. It should say who handles the power wiring, whether the price covers running power to the gate, and what happens to the old gate. Power wiring for a gate opener is electrical work, so ask the installer who holds the electrical license.

  • Contractor checks: Texas has no state license category for fence contractors, though some cities register them, including Dallas, Richardson and Irving. Ask for city registration and proof of insurance.
  • Dallas permit: the City says a fence permit is required above 4 ft in a front yard or 6 ft elsewhere, and its DallasNow guide asks that a general contractor be listed on fence applications. Confirm with the City whether your gate job needs one.
  • Visibility triangle: Dallas restricts any item between 2-1/2 ft and 8 ft above the curb near corners (45 ft along each curb line) and at driveway and alley edges (20 ft). Ask the contractor to check this against your lot.
  • HOA: under Texas Property Code Sec. 202.023 an association can still regulate fence type and may require a driveway gate set back at least 10 feet from the right-of-way on a laned roadway. Get written approval first.
  • Digging: new gate posts or track foundations mean digging. Texas811 says the contractor is responsible for calling 811 two business days before.

Rules differ by city, so check the page for yours: Plano, Garland, Richardson, Mesquite, Irving or Carrollton. Confirm with the City and your HOA before you commit. Call now at (214) 555-0137, then compare two or three written quotes.

faq.q: How much does gate repair cost in Dallas?
faq.a: It depends on the fault. TX Fence & Deck lists a latch or hinge fix at $60 to $150, and Roof Raiders & Co in Dallas lists gate hardware and drop at $400 to $1,200. No Dallas firm we found publishes a service-call fee, so ask whether the visit is billed, and get two or three written quotes for the same fault.

faq.q: Why does my automatic gate stop, reverse or not close?
faq.a: Common causes to rule out are blocked or misaligned photo-eyes, limit settings, a sagging gate that binds, dead remote or backup batteries, and a power fault. Viking Fence in Austin lists opener repair at $150 to $400, motor repair at $200 to $600 and motor replacement at $500 to $1,200. TX Fence & Deck puts motor replacements at $1,000+.

faq.q: How much does a new automatic driveway gate cost in Dallas?
faq.a: TX Fence & Deck (28 Sep 2026) lists swing at $3,500 to $7,000, track slide at $4,500 to $8,500 and cantilever slide at $5,500 to $10,000, with most Dallas-area installs at $3,500 to $10,000. It says running power to a remote gate can add $500 to $2,000. The same firm's earlier page lists a single swing gate from $1,800, so prices vary widely; Fixr's national guide gives $2,500 to $5,500 with a $4,000 average.

faq.q: Do I need a permit or HOA approval to replace a gate?
faq.a: The City of Dallas requires a fence permit above 4 ft in a front yard or 6 ft elsewhere, so confirm with the City whether a gate-only job qualifies. Plano says repairs to existing fences under 25% of the fence area in 12 months need no permit. Texas Property Code Sec. 202.023 still lets an HOA regulate fence type, so get written approval before you start.

faq.q: Who should do the electrical work on an automatic gate opener?
faq.a: Power wiring for a gate opener is electrical work, so ask the installer who holds the electrical license. Have the quote say who runs the power and whether running power to a remote gate is included, since one Dallas-area firm says that can add $500 to $2,000. Do not accept a quote that leaves the wiring unassigned.
